detail.longDescription: I have this API which should get all items from Item table that pattern matches in WantedItem table that Item.item_id doesn’t exist in Table_3.item_id . @app.get("/wanted_items/{user_id}") def all_wanted_items(*, session: Session = Depends(get_session), user_id: UUID): get_all_items = session.exec( select(Item, WantedItem, Table_3) .where(WantedItem.user_id == user_id) .where(Item.item_id != Table_3.item_id) .where(col(Item.title).ilike(f"%{WantedItem.title}%")) ).all() if not get_all_items : raise HTTPException( status_code=404, detail="Some content", ) return [ { "item": item.model_dump(), "wanted_item": {"title":wanted_item.title}, "table_3": table_3.job_id, } for (item, wanted_item, table_3) in get_all_items ] My expectation of what it should return is this (before it, it should check if that item_id is already added to Table_3 . If yes then it should not include in list: [ { "items": [{ "item_id": "uuid", "title": "Computer ABC", },{ "item_id":"uuid", "title":"Computer Z" } ], "wanted_item": { "wanted_item_id": "str", "title": "Computer" }, }, { "items": [{ "item_id": "uuid", "title": "Playstation 5", },{ "item_id":"uuid", "title":"Playstation 3" } ], "wanted_item": { "wanted_item_id": "str", "title": "playstation" }, }, When I test my API I get: HTTPException: "Some content" What would be appropriate solution to this?
